source_text: Εξ ἀρχῆς γὰρ ὑμῖν ἔθος ἐστὶ τοῦτο, πάντας μὲν ἀδελφοὺς ποικίλως εὐεργετεῖν, ἐκκλησίαις τε πολλαῖς ταῖς κατὰ πᾶσαν πόλιν ἐφόδια πέμπειν· ὧδε μὲν τὴν τῶν δεομένων πενίαν ἀναψύχοντας· ἐν μετάλλοις δὲ ἀδελφοῖς ὑπάρχουσιν ἐπιχορηγοῦντας· δἰ ὧν πέμπετε ἀρχῆθεν ἐφοδίων, πατροπαράδοτον ἔθος Ῥωμαίων Ῥωμαῖοι διαφυλάττοντες· ὃ οὐ μόνον διατετήρηκεν ὁ μακάριος ὑμῶν ἐπίσκοπος Σωτὴρ, ἀλλὰ καὶ ἐπηύξηκεν· ἐπιχορηγῶν μὲν τὴν διαπεμπομένην δαψίλειαν τὴν εἰς τοὺς ἁγίους· λόγοις δὲ μακαρίοις τοὺς ἀνιόντας ἀδελφοὺς ὡς τέκνα πατὴρ φιλόστοργος παρακαλῶν. Hæc attulit Eusebius lib. iv. Hist. c. 23.
thought_title: Rome's inherited custom of aid, kept and increased by Soter
orientation: Dionysius of Corinth is praising the Roman church, in a passage quoted by Eusebius, for its long-standing custom of sending aid to needy brethren and churches.
pass_a_gloss: For from the beginning this is a custom for you, to benefit all brethren in various ways, and to send aid to many churches in every city; here refreshing the poverty of those in need; and supplying brethren who are in the mines; through the aid which you send from the beginning, Romans preserving a custom handed down from the fathers of the Romans; which not only has the blessed bishop of yours Soter kept, but also has increased; supplying the abundance sent out to the saints; and with blessed words exhorting the brethren who come up as a father who loves his children.

choices.why: Glossary term; renders the travel provisions or supplies sent to needy churches.

choices.english: a custom handed down from the fathers of the Romans
choices.why: Keeps the genitive Ῥωμαίων as source of the custom, matching the source's emphasis on inherited Roman practice.

choices.english: the blessed bishop of yours Soter
choices.why: Preserves the word order and the possessive force of ὑμῶν, showing Soter as the Romans' bishop.

choices.english: as a father who loves his children
choices.why: Renders φιλόστοργος with its specific sense of parental affection, keeping the simile's force.
rejected: like a father fond of his children

pass_b_english: From the beginning you have had this custom: to benefit all the brethren in various ways, and to send aid to many churches in every city. In some places you refresh the poverty of those in need; in others you supply the brethren who are in the mines. By the aid you have sent from the beginning, you Romans preserve a custom handed down from the fathers of the Romans. Your blessed bishop Soter has not only kept this custom, but has increased it, supplying the abundance that is sent to the saints, and exhorting the brethren who come to him with blessed words, as a father who loves his children.
